-- Table 1: user_tokens
-- Description: Manages one-time security tokens for email verification, password reset, magic link authentication, and account recovery. Includes expiration tracking, usage logging, and comprehensive audit trails for forensic analysis. Each record captures essential metadata including issuance timestamps, expiration deadlines, consumption status, and cryptographic validation hashes. The table enforces strict lifecycle controls to ensure tokens are automatically invalidated after single-use or expiration, preventing replay attacks and maintaining robust account security across all authentication workflows.
-- Business Case: Secure account actions require time-limited, single-use tokens that cannot be reused or replayed by malicious actors. This table centralizes token management across all authentication flows, ensuring consistent security policies are enforced platform-wide. The design meticulously tracks the entire lifecycle of each token, from initial creation through successful validation or automatic expiration. Separate token types enable differentiated validity periods tailored to specific risk profiles; for instance, password reset tokens are configured with a one-hour lifespan, email verification tokens last twenty-four hours, and magic link authentication tokens expire after just fifteen minutes. This granular approach ensures that compromised tokens have a minimal window of exploitation. Furthermore, the system enforces automatic invalidation of all existing tokens whenever a user changes their password, effectively neutralizing any previously stolen credentials. Comprehensive audit logging of token usage, including IP addresses and user agents, provides security teams with the forensic data necessary to investigate suspicious account recovery attempts or brute-force attacks. The inclusion of rate-limiting metrics and attempt counters allows the platform to automatically lock out malicious actors attempting to guess valid tokens, thereby protecting user accounts from automated credential stuffing and enumeration attacks.
-- KPIs: Token usage rate (percentage of issued tokens successfully used), Average time to use (median time between issuance and consumption), Token expiration rate (percentage of tokens expiring unused), Token reuse attempts (count of validation attempts after consumption), Fraud detection rate (percentage of anomalous token patterns flagged).
-- Feature Reference: AUTH07 (Token-based Authentication), AUTH08 (Email Verification), AUTH09 (Password Reset), SEC27 (Session Management)

-- Table 2: user_login_history
-- Description: Detailed log of all login attempts (success/failure) with rich contextual metadata including IP addresses, user agents, device fingerprints, geolocation coordinates, and failure reasons. Supports advanced security analytics, real-time threat detection, and regulatory compliance auditing. Each record provides a complete snapshot of the authentication event, enabling security teams to reconstruct login sequences, identify compromised accounts, and detect anomalous access patterns. The table is partitioned by date to ensure optimal query performance even when storing billions of historical authentication records across multi-tenant environments.
-- Business Case: Comprehensive login logging is essential for detecting brute-force attacks, account takeover attempts, and unusual access patterns before they result in data breaches. This table captures every authentication event with enough detail to reconstruct the user's login history, identify compromised accounts, and meet stringent compliance requirements such as SOC2, GDPR, and ISO27001. The data feeds directly into Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems and enables real-time alerting on suspicious patterns, such as multiple consecutive failures from geographically disparate IP addresses or impossible travel scenarios. By correlating login history with device fingerprints, the platform can automatically flag unfamiliar devices and trigger step-up authentication challenges. Partitioning by date ensures that historical queries remain performant without degrading real-time authentication throughput. Additionally, the table supports automated threat intelligence integration, cross-referencing login IPs against known malicious databases to proactively block credential stuffing campaigns. The granular failure reason tracking enables product teams to optimize the login experience by identifying common user errors, reducing support ticket volume related to access issues, and improving overall platform usability while maintaining enterprise-grade security posture.
-- KPIs: Login success rate (percentage of successful vs. failed attempts), Unique IPs per user (average number of distinct IPs per user), Impossible travel incidents (logins from geographically impossible locations within short timeframes), Brute force detection (accounts with >5 failed attempts in 5 minutes), Device churn (rate of new device registrations per user per month).
-- Feature Reference: SEC18 (Login Monitoring), SEC19 (Anomaly Detection), SEC30 (Threat Intelligence), AUD09 (Access Audit)

-- Table 3: user_password_history
-- Description: Stores cryptographically hashed historical passwords to enforce password rotation policies and prevent credential reuse. Fully supports NIST SP 800-63B compliance guidelines. Each entry maintains a secure, irreversible hash of previous passwords along with metadata indicating when the password was last changed and by whom. The table enables configurable history depth (typically 5-24 previous passwords) to enforce organizational security policies. By maintaining this historical ledger, the platform ensures that users cannot cycle back to recently compromised or weak passwords, significantly reducing the risk of credential-based attacks and unauthorized account access.
-- Business Case: NIST guidelines and modern security best practices explicitly require that users cannot reuse recent passwords to prevent credential recycling attacks. This table maintains a configurable history length to enforce this policy seamlessly across all user accounts. When users initiate a password change, the system hashes the new credential and cross-references it against this historical table to prevent reuse. The design also tracks password age to enforce mandatory rotation intervals, ensuring that stale credentials are regularly refreshed. Historical data is critical for forensic investigations when credentials are compromised, allowing security teams to determine exactly when a compromised password was active and what systems it may have accessed. Additionally, the table integrates with breached password databases to proactively flag and block users from setting passwords that have already appeared in known data leaks. By combining historical hashing with breach intelligence, the platform dramatically reduces the attack surface for credential stuffing and password spraying campaigns. The table's audit trails also provide compliance evidence for regulatory auditors, demonstrating that the organization actively enforces strong credential hygiene practices. Automated alerts notify security teams when users repeatedly attempt to bypass rotation policies, enabling rapid intervention and targeted security awareness training.
-- KPIs: Password reuse rate (percentage of change attempts blocked due to history), Average password age (median time between password changes), Compliance rate (percentage of users with password age under 90 days), Breach impact reduction (accounts requiring forced reset after external breach), Rotation enforcement effectiveness (reduction in account takeover incidents).
-- Feature Reference: SEC19 (Password Policy), SEC32 (Credential Management), COMP13 (NIST Compliance), AUD11 (Credential Audit)

-- Table 4: user_anonymization_queue
-- Description: Asynchronously processes GDPR right-to-be-forgotten requests, tracking the status, progress, and execution details of data anonymization jobs. Provides a reliable state machine for coordinating multi-step erasure operations across distributed databases and third-party integrations. Each record captures job metadata, including target data scopes, processing stages, failure logs, and retry counters. The table ensures that sensitive erasure requests are handled systematically without blocking application performance, while maintaining complete auditability for regulatory compliance. Automated cleanup routines and escalation pathways guarantee that delayed or failed anonymization tasks receive prompt administrative attention.
-- Business Case: GDPR Article 17 requires complete erasure of personal data upon user request. However, immediate synchronous deletion can severely impact system performance and may need careful coordination across multiple microservices, caches, and external data processors. This queue decouples the legal request from technical execution, allowing the platform to retry logic, track progress, and maintain comprehensive auditability. The design supports complex multi-step anonymization processes, such as pseudonymizing user profiles before archiving order history, and finally purging raw event logs. Dependency tracking ensures referential integrity is maintained throughout the erasure lifecycle. Failed jobs are automatically retried with exponential backoff, and critical failures trigger immediate alerts to the data privacy team. The table integrates seamlessly with data retention policies and legal hold registries, ensuring that erasure requests are automatically paused when data is under active litigation or regulatory investigation. This intelligent routing prevents accidental destruction of evidence while demonstrating to auditors that the platform has robust, automated mechanisms for honoring data subject rights. Historical job data enables continuous improvement of anonymization algorithms and helps privacy teams forecast processing capacity during peak request periods.
-- KPIs: Average completion time (mean days from request submission to full anonymization), Queue backlog (number of pending anonymization jobs), Success rate (percentage of jobs completed without manual intervention), Retry frequency (average retries executed per failed job), Deadline compliance (percentage of requests completed within the 30-day GDPR window).
-- Feature Reference: GDPR10 (Right to Erasure), GDPR16 (Data Anonymization), BATCH02 (Batch Processing), AUD13 (Erasure Audit)

-- Table 5: user_export_files
-- Description: Stores metadata and delivery information for generated data export files related to data portability requests and user-initiated downloads. Tracks file formats, storage locations, expiration schedules, and download histories. Each record links directly to a specific user and export request, capturing technical details like checksum verification, compression ratios, and generation timestamps. The table ensures secure, auditable handling of personal data packages while enforcing strict retention policies to prevent indefinite exposure. Download tracking provides granular visibility into how users access their exported data, supporting both compliance reporting and user experience optimization.
-- Business Case: GDPR Article 20 grants users the fundamental right to receive their personal data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format. This table serves as the operational backbone for fulfilling these portability requests, managing the entire lifecycle from generation through secure delivery and eventual secure deletion. Files are generated asynchronously, packaged in multiple formats (JSON, CSV, XML), and stored in encrypted, access-controlled object storage with strict expiration policies. The table tracks every download event, including IP addresses and timestamps, providing a complete audit trail that proves data was securely delivered and not accessed by unauthorized parties. Automatic expiration ensures that temporary data packages do not become lingering security liabilities. Multiple format support accommodates different user technical proficiencies, from machine-readable JSON for developers to human-readable CSV for general users. The table also integrates with the consent management system to ensure that exported data accurately reflects the user's consent boundaries at the time of export. Download analytics help product teams understand which export formats are most popular, driving future platform development. Comprehensive logging of generation failures and retry attempts ensures high reliability, while checksum verification guarantees data integrity throughout the transfer process, protecting both the organization and the user from data corruption claims.
-- KPIs: Export request volume (number of portability requests processed per month), Average file size (mean megabytes per generated data package), Download completion rate (percentage of exports successfully downloaded by users), Generation time (average duration from request initiation to file readiness), Format popularity (distribution of requested export formats by user segment).
-- Feature Reference: GDPR17 (Data Portability), GDPR18 (Export Management), AUD14 (Export Audit), DPP02 (Data Portability)

-- Table 6: user_security_events
-- Description: Comprehensive logging of security-sensitive user and system events for SIEM integration, threat detection, and forensic analysis. Captures authentication changes, permission modifications, role assignments, and suspicious activity patterns. Each record includes contextual metadata such as originating IP, user agent, session ID, and detailed event payload. The table supports real-time alerting pipelines and automated incident response workflows. Partitioned by month to ensure high-throughput ingestion and efficient historical querying, this table forms the critical data foundation for the platform's security operations center and compliance reporting infrastructure.
-- Business Case: Modern security operations require centralized, high-fidelity logging of all security-relevant events to detect, investigate, and respond to threats before they cause harm. This table serves as the primary ingestion point for security telemetry, capturing critical actions like MFA device changes, administrative privilege escalations, API key revocations, and unusual data access patterns. The design supports industry-standard log formats (CEF, LEEF) for seamless integration with enterprise SIEM platforms like Splunk, Sentinel, and ELK. Partitioning by month ensures that the platform can maintain years of security telemetry without degrading query performance for active investigations. Real-time streaming of these events to alerting engines enables automated response actions, such as temporarily locking accounts exhibiting credential stuffing behavior or requiring step-up verification when access patterns deviate from established baselines. The table also provides crucial evidence for regulatory audits, demonstrating that the organization actively monitors and logs security-critical operations as required by SOC2, ISO27001, and GDPR. By correlating events across users, sessions, and IP addresses, security analysts can reconstruct attack timelines, identify lateral movement patterns, and quantify the blast radius of potential breaches. Historical trend analysis from this data helps prioritize security investments, revealing which attack vectors are most frequently attempted and which controls are most effective at mitigating them.
-- KPIs: Event volume by type (number of security events generated per category daily), Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) (average time from event occurrence to alert generation), Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) (average time from alert to initial remediation action), Event correlation rate (percentage of isolated events successfully linked to broader incidents), False positive rate (percentage of security alerts determined to be non-threatening after investigation).
-- Feature Reference: SEC35 (Security Event Monitoring), SEC36 (SIEM Integration), INC03 (Incident Detection), COMP17 (Security Logging)

-- Table 7: data_processing_records
-- Description: Comprehensive Record of Processing Activities (RoPA) as mandated by GDPR Article 30. Documents each data processing operation, including lawful basis, data categories, retention periods, security measures, and third-party transfers. Provides a centralized inventory enabling compliance reporting, risk assessment, and regulatory accountability. Each record captures controller information, processing purposes, data subject categories, recipient details, and cross-border transfer mechanisms. The table supports versioning and periodic reviews to ensure processing documentation remains current and accurately reflects organizational data practices. Automated validation rules flag inconsistencies and missing required fields before records are finalized.
-- Business Case: GDPR strictly requires all data controllers to maintain a detailed, accurate, and up-to-date record of all personal data processing activities. This table serves as the authoritative source of truth for the organization's data mapping initiative, enabling legal and compliance teams to quickly generate documentation for supervisory authority inquiries, data protection impact assessments, and breach notifications. The structured design ensures that all mandatory Article 30 elements are captured systematically: processing purposes, categories of data subjects, data categories, recipient categories, international transfer safeguards, and technical security measures. Versioning capabilities allow organizations to track how processing activities evolve over time, providing historical context for auditors. The table integrates with the data retention scheduler and consent registry to automatically validate that processing activities have documented lawful bases and approved retention periods. Cross-referencing capabilities enable impact analysis when third-party vendors change their security postures or when new regulatory requirements emerge. The inventory also supports privacy-by-design initiatives by forcing product teams to document processing purposes and data minimization strategies before features launch. Regular review workflows ensure that stale processing activities are archived or updated, preventing compliance drift. By centralizing processing documentation, the organization reduces legal risk, streamlines regulatory audits, and builds a transparent data culture that demonstrates accountability to users and regulators alike.
-- KPIs: Processing activity coverage (percentage of active data flows fully documented in the registry), Review compliance (percentage of records reviewed and validated within the policy period), Risk assessment completion (percentage of activities with documented DPIA references and risk levels), Transfer tracking (number of international data transfers documented with valid legal mechanisms), Data subject coverage (count of unique data subject categories processed per active record).
-- Feature Reference: GDPR07 (Processing Activities), COMP03 (Data Inventory)

-- Table 8: consent_audit_logs
-- Description: Immutable, append-only log capturing every consent event including grants, revocations, updates, and automatic expirations. Provides complete forensic evidence for GDPR Article 7(1) compliance requirements regarding demonstrable consent. Each record stores precise timestamps, originating IP addresses, user agent strings, consent form versions, and state transitions. The design ensures absolute integrity of consent history by preventing updates or deletions, while partitioning by month maintains optimal performance for high-volume auditing. The table supports legal dispute resolution by providing unalterable proof of exactly what a user consented to, when, and how.
-- Business Case: GDPR mandates that controllers must be able to demonstrate that valid consent was freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous. This table provides an unalterable audit trail of every consent action, capturing the exact moment consent was granted or withdrawn, along with the technical context in which it occurred. The design deliberately separates historical consent events from current consent states to ensure immutability and prevent any possibility of retroactive alteration. Each log entry includes cryptographic hashes of the consent form version presented to the user, proving exactly which terms and conditions were accepted. IP address and user agent logging enables security teams to investigate fraudulent consent generation or bot-driven consent manipulation. The table supports automated compliance reporting by aggregating consent withdrawal rates, geographic distributions, and policy version adoption metrics. In the event of regulatory investigations or user disputes, this table provides instant access to complete consent histories without relying on potentially incomplete application-level logs. Partitioning by month ensures that even platforms with millions of daily users can query consent histories efficiently without degrading transactional performance. The audit trail also feeds into automated marketing suppression systems, ensuring that users who withdraw consent are immediately excluded from future communications across all channels. By maintaining rigorous consent documentation, the organization minimizes legal liability, builds user trust, and demonstrates proactive commitment to privacy rights.
-- KPIs: Consent event volume (total number of consent actions logged per operational period), Withdrawal rate (percentage of granted consents subsequently revoked by users), Geographic distribution (percentage breakdown of consent events by user country or region), Policy version adoption (distribution of consent grants across different policy versions), Audit trail completeness (percentage of user accounts with continuous, unbroken consent documentation).
-- Feature Reference: GDPR06 (Consent Management), AUD20 (Consent Audit)

-- Table 9: privacy_request_workflows
-- Description: Tracks the complete end-to-end lifecycle of Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR), including identity verification, scope assessment, data collection, review, fulfillment, and closure. Provides structured workflow management to ensure timely, compliant responses to user privacy requests. Each record captures assignment details, status transitions, deadline tracking, escalation paths, and fulfillment methods. The table integrates with data subject request intake systems, anonymization queues, and legal hold registries to provide seamless cross-functional coordination. Automated notifications and SLA monitoring ensure that privacy teams can manage high request volumes while maintaining strict regulatory deadlines.
-- Business Case: GDPR requires timely, comprehensive responses to data subject requests, typically within one calendar month. This table provides a centralized workflow engine to manage each request from initial receipt through final certification, ensuring consistent handling across all privacy team members. The design enforces strict status transitions, requiring identity verification before scoping begins, and scope approval before data collection starts. Integration with the user_anonymization_queue ensures that erasure requests trigger appropriate technical jobs automatically. The table tracks complex scenarios where requests must be partially fulfilled due to legal holds or third-party dependencies, documenting exactly what data was provided, withheld, or anonymized. Escalation pathways automatically notify senior privacy counsel when requests approach SLA deadlines or involve high-risk jurisdictions. Internal collaboration features allow team members to attach notes, evidence, and legal opinions directly to the workflow record. The table also generates audit-ready reports showing processing times, fulfillment methods, and exception reasons for regulatory submission. By standardizing the DSAR process, the organization reduces response errors, minimizes legal exposure from missed deadlines, and provides users with transparent, consistent privacy experiences. Historical workflow data enables continuous process improvement, revealing bottlenecks in data discovery or verification that can be addressed through automation or additional training.
-- KPIs: Average fulfillment time (median days from request submission to final completion), SLA compliance rate (percentage of requests completed within the legal deadline), Backlog volume (number of open requests grouped by age and complexity), Escalation rate (percentage of requests requiring management or legal escalation), Request complexity distribution (percentage breakdown by request type, jurisdiction, and data volume).
-- Feature Reference: GDPR01 (Data Subject Rights), WF06 (DSAR Workflow)

-- Table 10: data_retention_schedules
-- Description: Defines automated data retention rules for specific data categories, specifying retention periods, legal bases, and actions upon expiry. Implements GDPR Article 5(1)(e) storage limitation principle through configurable policy management. Each record links retention rules to specific tables, columns, or data categories, with support for multiple trigger mechanisms and exception handling. The table drives scheduled cleanup jobs that automatically delete, anonymize, or archive data when retention periods expire. Version control and review tracking ensure that retention policies remain aligned with evolving regulatory requirements and organizational risk tolerance.
-- Business Case: Privacy regulations explicitly require that personal data be kept no longer than necessary for the purposes for which it was processed. This table operationalizes that principle by providing a centralized, enforceable framework for data lifecycle management. Each retention rule specifies the exact data scope, the legal or operational basis for retention, the duration, and the required action upon expiry (deletion, anonymization, or archival). The system supports multiple trigger mechanisms, allowing retention periods to be calculated from creation dates, last user activity, or specific business events. Exception handling integrates with legal hold systems, ensuring that data under active litigation or regulatory investigation is automatically protected from automated deletion. Automated enforcement jobs read these schedules daily, generating audit reports showing which records were purged, anonymized, or archived. This proactive approach drastically reduces the organization's data liability surface, minimizes storage costs, and eliminates manual retention tracking. Versioning capabilities allow legal teams to test new retention policies in staging environments before production deployment. Regular review workflows ensure that outdated policies are updated as regulations change or business processes evolve. By maintaining rigorous, automated retention controls, the organization demonstrates proactive compliance, reduces breach exposure from obsolete data, and builds a scalable data governance foundation that grows alongside the platform.
-- KPIs: Rule coverage (percentage of active data assets governed by explicit retention schedules), Enforcement success rate (percentage of scheduled retention actions completed without error), Data volume reduction (total gigabytes deleted or anonymized per policy cycle), Exception frequency (number of legal holds or manual overrides applied to active schedules), Compliance audit pass rate (percentage of retention policies validated as compliant during external audits).
-- Feature Reference: GDPR05 (Data Retention), RET01 (Retention Rules)


-- Table 51: database_migration_history

-- Business Case: Enterprise platforms require strict version control for schema changes to prevent deployment conflicts, enable rapid rollbacks, and maintain compliance with change management policies. This table centralizes migration history, allowing DevOps teams to verify script integrity via SHA-256 checksums, monitor execution performance, and audit who applied which change. Integration with CI/CD pipelines ensures that only validated, approved migrations reach production.
-- KPIs: Migration success rate, Average execution time per migration, Rollback frequency, Checksum validation pass rate, Deployment pipeline compliance %.
-- Feature Reference: OPS01 (Schema Management), DEV03 (CI/CD Integration), COMP04 (Change Auditing)
